intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD; 606761) on chromosome 16q23.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MLYCD gene, which encodes malonyl-CoA decarboxylase.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
checks.explanation: The paper reports only homozygous mutations. Compound heterozygosity is not addressed.

checks.claim: The MLYCD gene is located on chromosome 16q23.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not give a chromosomal location for the gene. It might be in the full text.

paragraphs.text: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism. Its biochemical hallmark is increased urinary excretion of malonic acid (malonic aciduria). Clinical features vary. They include developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, vomiting and diarrhea, and cardiomyopathy. Malonyl-CoA inhibits carnitine palmitoyltransferase I, so its accumulation is thought to impair mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is a rare inborn error of metabolism.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MCD) deficiency is an extremely rare inborn error of metabolism
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The biochemical hallmark of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is increased urinary excretion of malonic acid (malonic aciduria).
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria
checks.explanation: Malonic aciduria is the characterizing feature.

checks.claim: The clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency vary.
checks.evidence_quote: presents with metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and/or cardiomyopathy. Patients also show neurological signs and symptoms that have been infrequently reported.
checks.explanation: The phrase 'and/or' implies the presentation varies, but the abstract does not say outright that the clinical features vary.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: a lethal disorder characterized by cardiomyopathy and developmental delay
checks.explanation: Developmental delay named as a feature.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: deficiency of the enzyme has been associated with mild mental retardation, seizures, hypotonia

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy
checks.explanation: Seizure disorder is listed.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include hypoglycemia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy
checks.explanation: Hypoglycemia is listed.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include metabolic acidosis.
checks.evidence_quote: presents with metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and/or cardiomyopathy
checks.explanation: Metabolic acidosis is listed as a presenting feature.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include vomiting.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with vomiting, a seizure, hypoglycaemia and mild metabolic acidosis during a urinary tract infection
checks.explanation: The patient presented with vomiting.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include diarrhea.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not mention diarrhea.

checks.claim: Clinical features of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: a lethal disorder characterized by cardiomyopathy and developmental delay

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA inhibits carnitine palmitoyltransferase I.
checks.evidence_quote: tissues in which cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA is a potent inhibitor of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation
checks.explanation: Abstract states malonyl-CoA inhibits mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation but does not name carnitine palmitoyltransferase I.

checks.claim: Accumulation of malonyl-CoA in malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is thought to impair mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.
checks.evidence_quote: Cytoplasmic MCD is positioned to play a role in the regulation of cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA abundance and, thus, of mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation. This hypothesis is supported by the fact that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patients display a number of phenotypes that are reminiscent of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders.
checks.explanation: The abstract presents this as a hypothesis, which matches the claim's 'thought to'.

paragraphs.text: The disorder has also been called malonic aciduria and MLYCD deficiency.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency has also been called malonic aciduria.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The term 'malonic aciduria' does not appear in the abstract.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency has also been called MLYCD deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: The term MLYCD deficiency is used.

paragraphs.text: Brown et al. (1984) were among the first to describe malonic aciduria with deficient malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity, in a child with developmental delay and episodes of metabolic decompensation.

checks.claim: Brown et al. (1984) were among the first to describe malonic aciduria with deficient malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: A patient is described with a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme, malonyl CoA decarboxylase - an inborn error of metabolism not recognized previously.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports this as the first recognition of the deficiency.

checks.claim: Brown et al. (1984) described a child with malonic aciduria and deficient malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity who had developmental delay.
checks.explanation: Developmental delay is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Brown et al. (1984) described a child with malonic aciduria and deficient malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity who had episodes of metabolic decompensation.
checks.evidence_quote: a child with repeated episodes of vomiting, some requiring hospitalization
checks.explanation: The abstract describes repeated vomiting episodes needing hospitalization, not explicitly 'metabolic decompensation'.

paragraphs.text: Salomons et al. (2007) described the clinical, enzymatic and molecular findings in additional patients with MLYCD deficiency. They emphasized how variable the phenotype is: findings included developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, hypoglycemia and cardiomyopathy.

checks.claim: Salomons et al. (2007) described clinical, enzymatic and molecular findings in additional patients with MLYCD deficiency.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. This claim is about Salomons et al. (2007), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Salomons et al. (2007) emphasized that the phenotype of MLYCD deficiency is highly variable.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. This claim is about Salomons et al. (2007), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Patients with MLYCD deficiency described by Salomons et al. (2007) had findings including developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, hypoglycemia and cardiomyopathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. This claim is about Salomons et al. (2007), which this paper does not address.

paragraphs.text: Affected individuals excrete increased amounts of malonic acid in urine. Some also have mildly increased methylmalonic acid. Malonylcarnitine is raised in blood, so the disorder can be detected by acylcarnitine analysis, including newborn screening. Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity is deficient in cultured fibroblasts.

checks.claim: Individuals with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency excrete increased amounts of malonic acid in urine.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria
checks.explanation: Malonic aciduria means increased urinary malonic acid.

checks.claim: Some individuals with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency have mildly increased urinary methylmalonic acid.
checks.evidence_quote: The urine contained increased amounts of malonic, methylmalonic, succinic, adipic, glutaric and suberic acids.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports increased urinary methylmalonic acid but does not describe the increase as mild.

checks.claim: Malonylcarnitine is raised in the blood of individuals with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not mention malonylcarnitine.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency can be detected by acylcarnitine analysis, including newborn screening.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not mention acylcarnitine analysis or newborn screening.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity is deficient in cultured fibroblasts from individuals with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitochondrial malonyl CoA decarboxylase activity in cultured fibroblast extracts was 4% of the mean control value.
checks.explanation: Enzyme activity in the patient's cultured fibroblasts was 4% of the control mean.

paragraphs.text: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. Patients carry homozygous or compound heterozygous MLYCD mutations.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency carry homozygous or compound heterozygous MLYCD mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD)
checks.explanation: Only homozygous mutations are reported. Compound heterozygosity is not addressed.

paragraphs.text: Sacksteder et al. (1999) and FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified mutations in the MLYCD gene in patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.

checks.claim: Sacksteder et al. (1999) identified mutations in the MLYCD gene in patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: a malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patient has a severe mutation in the MCD gene (c.947-948delTT)
checks.explanation: Abstract describes a single patient with one mutation, not mutations in several patients.

checks.claim: FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified mutations in the MLYCD gene in patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
checks.explanation: The paper identified MLYCD mutations in patients with MCD deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Salomons et al. (2007) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous MLYCD mutations in further patients with the deficiency.

checks.claim: Salomons et al. (2007) identified homozygous or compound heterozygous MLYCD mutations in further patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. This claim is about Salomons et al. (2007), which this paper does not address.

paragraphs.text: Reported treatments include a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet and carnitine supplementation. Some patients with cardiomyopathy improved on this treatment.

checks.claim: Reported treatments for malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet.
checks.evidence_quote: Only relatively small quantities of malonic, methylmalonic and succinic acid were excreted in the urine when the boy was fed an isocaloric low fat, high carbohydrate diet.
checks.explanation: The abstract shows that a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet reduced organic acid excretion in a dietary study of one patient. It does not present the diet as a reported treatment.

checks.claim: Reported treatments for malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency include carnitine supplementation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss treatment.

checks.claim: Some patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency and cardiomyopathy improved on a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet with carnitine supplementation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 9 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss treatment or cardiomyopathy outcomes.
